findings.evidence: <button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button> sits between the Preferred contact time field and the Date of birth fieldset, while the primary submit button, <button id="submit-btn" type="submit">Create account</button>, carries no style at all.
findings.fix: Remove View details from the field column, or move it to a clearly secondary position beside Create account at the end of the form, and drop its padding and font-size so it reads as visibly lesser than the primary action.
findings.violation: A secondary action is styled more prominently than the primary action and sits above a required group of fields, so a person can mistake it for the way to finish the form.

findings.evidence: <select id="dob-day-select" autocomplete="bday-day" required=""> <select id="dob-month-select" autocomplete="bday-month" required=""> <select id="dob-year-select" autocomplete="bday-year" required="">
findings.fix: Use three short text fields for day, month and year, with the numeric input mode.
findings.violation: A date the person knows by heart is picked from three drop-downs, the year from 60 options.

findings.evidence: The page's heading is "Create your account" and its submit button reads "Create account", yet the form requires: Company website (#website-input, line 37), Membership number (#member-input, line 41), Account number (#acctnum-input, line 45), Organization name (#org-input, line 67), Preferred contact time (#contacttime-input, line 71), and a full Date of birth (#dob-day-select and its month and year selects, lines 77 to 187). None of these answers is used by, or explained in connection with, creating a personal account; Membership number and Account number in particular ask a person who is creating an account for identifiers that an account not yet created cannot have.
findings.fix: Drop Company website, Organization name, Preferred contact time and Date of birth from account creation; ask for them later only where a specific feature needs the answer. Remove Membership number and Account number, or make them optional and explain, beside the field, that they are for linking an existing membership rather than for the new account.
findings.violation: The form requires several fields that creating an account does not use, with no stated reason for any of them.

findings.evidence: <input id="postal-input" name="postal_code" type="text" autocomplete="postal-code" required="" size="3"> (size=3)
findings.fix: Size the field to show at least 5 characters.
findings.violation: This postal code field shows 3 characters, too few to show a typical value whole while it is typed and checked.

findings.fix: Loosen the pattern to accept every valid way of writing the value, and normalise it after submission.
findings.violation: The pattern on this phone field rejects valid values such as +44 20 7946 0958; 020 7946 0958.

findings.evidence: <label id="name-label" for="name-input">Full name</label> (line 11) and <label id="legalname-label" for="legalname-input">Your name</label> (line 62) are both plain name fields (autocomplete="name" on each) with no stated distinction between them.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate field, or, if the two values can genuinely differ, relabel the second one to say how (for example "Legal name, if different from above") and make it optional.
findings.violation: The form asks for the person's name twice under two different labels, so the person must decide whether the second answer should repeat the first or differ from it.

findings.evidence: font-size: 13px declared by its inline style
findings.fix: Set the field's font size to at least 16 pixels.
findings.violation: The text in this field is 13 pixels, below the 16 pixels at which a phone stops zooming the page on focus.
This web address field is type text, so a phone does not show the keyboard built for it.
